nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
It is related from Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the meaning of
سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ, and he said: "Declaring Allah free of every evil." Abū Jaʿfar said: the explanation of this is that it means putting Allah, Mighty and Majestic, far away from everything the idolaters ascribed to Him of rivals, opposites, partners and children. According to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them both, it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. سبّحت الله تسبيحا ("I declared Allah's transcendence with a declaring"); except that when it stands alone it is definite and accusative without tanwīn (nunation), because at its end there are two added letters and it is definite. Sībawayh reported that some of the Arabs make it indefinite and so make it fully declinable. Abū ʿUbayd reported two other ways of explaining its accusative besides this: that it is accusative as a vocative, i.e. يا سبحان الله; and the other way: that it is not qualified. الَّذِي is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). And he said: سرى and أسرى are two well-known dialectal usages. بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا: ليلا is an adverb (ẓarf). مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ: الحرام is a naʿt (adjective) of المسجد. The root sense of حرام is prevention; so the Sacred Mosque is one in which hunting is prohibited. Abū Isḥāq said: the whole sacred precinct (al-ḥaram) is also called a mosque. إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى: الأقصى is a naʿt of it, and likewise الَّذِي بارَكْنا حَوْلَهُ. It is said: the meaning of "We blessed its surroundings" is that the prophets, peace be upon them, who came after Moses ﷺ from the Children of Israel were in Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) and its surroundings, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, blessed those places by keeping idolatry far from them; and for this reason it was named Bayt al-Maqdis, because it was sanctified (quddisa), i.e. purified, from idolatry. لِنُرِيَهُ is accusative by the lām of purpose (lām kay), which stands in place of أن; its origin is the lām of the genitive.

nahhas-irab:2-3.t: وَآتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ: two objects; and likewise وَجَعَلْناهُ هُدىً لِبَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ. أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُوا with yāʾ «[Translator's note: i.e. ألّا يتّخذوا; the source prints the tāʾ form here.]» is the reading of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, the implied form being لئلا يتخذوا ("so that they should not take"). The reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries and the people of Kufa is أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُوا; Abū ʿUbayd claimed that it is on the basis of an omission, i.e. "We said to them: do not take". Abū Jaʿfar said: this needs no omission; «أنّ» «[Translator's note: so printed, with shadda; the discussion concerns أن.]» can have the meaning of أي ("that is"), and «أن» can be in the position of the accusative, the meaning being بأن لا تتخذوا ("that you should not take"). The speech was put in the second person because after it comes ذُرِّيَّةَ مَنْ حَمَلْنا in the second person. ذرية is accusative in four ways: it can be a vocative in construct; it can be a badal (substitute) for وكيل, since وكيل has a plural meaning; it and وكيل can be two objects, as you say: لا تتخذ زيدا صاحبا ("do not take Zayd as a companion"); and the fourth way is with the meaning أعني ("I mean"). The nominative is permissible on the reading of whoever read with yāʾ, as a badal for the wāw; but the badal for the wāw is not permissible on the reading of whoever read with tāʾ: one does not say كلّمتك زيدا nor كلمتني زيدا, because the addressee and the addresser need no clarification.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
وَقَضَيْنا إِلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ: we have mentioned the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, that its meaning is "We informed them".
The root sense of قضى in the language is doing a thing in a firm, decisive way; the judge (qāḍī) is the one who makes decisive matters that take effect, and al-qaḍāʾ is the decisive matter that takes effect and cannot be repelled. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Abū al-ʿĀliya read وَقَضَيْنا إِلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ فِي الْكِتابِ «[Translator's note: the variant reading is not visible in the printed text, which matches the ordinary reading.]», and it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, Jābir ibn Zayd and Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim that they read لَتُفْسِدُنَّ as a verb whose agent is not named (passive). «[Translator's note: i.e. لَتُفْسَدُنَّ; the source prints the ordinary vowelling.]» وَلَتَعْلُنَّ, i.e. you will surely become great; the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters and because what precedes it indicates it.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
فَإِذا جاءَ وَعْدُ أُولاهُما بَعَثْنا عَلَيْكُمْ عِباداً لَنا أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ: it is said: i.e. We left the way open between you and them. Al-Ḥasan read فجاسوا خلل الديار. Abū Isḥāq said: the root sense of الجوس is seeking a thing exhaustively, i.e. they searched to see whether they could find anyone they had not killed. خِلالَ is an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. in the midst of the dwellings.
وَكانَ وَعْداً مَفْعُولًا: وعدا is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and its noun is latent (muḍmar) in it.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: ثُمَّ رَدَدْنا لَكُمُ الْكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ, i.e. We gave you victory over them so that you returned to attack. وَجَعَلْناكُمْ أَكْثَرَ: two objects. نَفِيراً is by way of specification (bayān).

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
إِنْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ, i.e. the reward is yours; it is a protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَها, i.e. the punishment accrues to it. That لها means عليها is not said by the skilled grammarians; it is an inversion of meaning, and their citing as proof the ḥadīth «اشترطي الولاء لهم» ("stipulate the clientship for them") is worth nothing. There is disagreement over this ḥadīth: a group related it with this wording from the ḥadīth of Mālik ibn Anas, and it is al-Shāfiʿī's narration from him: «واشترطي الولاء لهم». This is a sound, clear meaning. One says اشترط الشيء when one makes it clear, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 266-
فأشرط فيها نفسه وهو معصم
(Gloss: "So he marked himself out in it [i.e. committed himself to the descent], while clinging fast.")
On the other narration «[Translator's note: the source prints the same wording again here; the other narration is presumably «واشرطي».]» the meaning of «واشترطي الولاء لهم» is "for their sake", as you say: "I honour So-and-so for you". There is another view on it: that it has the sense of a prohibition by way of threat and warning.
فَإِذا جاءَ وَعْدُ الْآخِرَةِ, i.e. the promise of the latter time; the adjective was put in the place of the noun it qualifies. The people of Medina and the people of Basra read لِيَسُوؤُا in the plural; the people of Kufa read ليسوء وجوهكم in the singular, except al-Kisāʾī, who read لنسوء وجوهكم and claimed it was the reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. From Ubayy ibn Kaʿb there are two narrations: one is that he read (لنسوءن وجوهكم), the lām with fatḥa — it is the lām of the oath with the light nūn, and the pause on it is with alif to distinguish the light from the heavy nūn; and it is related from him (ليسيء وجوهكم) with two yāʾs and a hamza. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The first reading, in the plural, is indicated by وَلِيَدْخُلُوا الْمَسْجِدَ كَما دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَلِيُتَبِّرُوا ما عَلَوْا. On the second reading there are three views: the meaning is "that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may disgrace"; al-Farrāʾ said: "that the punishment may disgrace"; Abū Isḥāq said: "that the promise may disgrace". The lām in both is the lām of purpose (lām kay), and so too in the third reading. There is an omission in the speech, the meaning being: "and when the promise of the latter time came, We sent them", so this verb is the reply of (إذا), and the lām kay is attached to it. On the meaning of "We sent them" there are two views: one is "We left the way open between you and them and did not make them fear you", so this is figurative: leaving the way open and not instilling fear was made a "sending"; similar to it is أَنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا الشَّياطِينَ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ [Maryam: 83]. The other view: "We sent them against you" means "We commanded them to make war on you when you disobeyed and caused corruption", and this is literal, not figurative. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that for whoever read ليسوآ وجوهكم it is, in his view, the reply without omission, but he implied a verb in «وليتبّروا». Qatāda said: the meaning is "and to destroy that over which they had risen"; someone else said: "and to destroy as long as they remain uppermost". Its true sense in Arabic is "to destroy during the time of their ascendancy", as you say: فلان يؤذيك ما ولي ("So-and-so harms you as long as he holds office").

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: عَسى رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يَرْحَمَكُمْ: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the mercy here is the sending of Muḥammad ﷺ. وَإِنْ عُدْتُمْ عُدْنا: it is said: if you return to disobedience, We return to withholding victory. وَجَعَلْنا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكافِرِينَ حَصِيراً: two objects.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: إِنَّ هذَا الْقُرْآنَ: القرآن is a naʿt (adjective) of هذا, and the khabar (predicate) is in يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ. وَيُبَشِّرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ: أنّ is in the position of the accusative, i.e. بأنّ ("with the news that").

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
وَيَدْعُ الْإِنْسانُ: the wāw was dropped in continuous recitation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. One should not pause on it, because in the written text (al-sawād) it is without wāw; and if someone paused on it outside the Qurʾan, he could only pause with the wāw, because it is the final radical (lām al-fiʿl), which is dropped only in the jussive or in continuous speech; and there is no alif after it. Likewise يدعو and يرجو: the alif comes only with the wāw of the plural, to distinguish it from the wāw that is the final radical in the singular. Al-Akhfash said: it comes in the plural to distinguish it from the wāw of conjunction. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: it comes to distinguish between the accusative pronoun and the emphasising one.
دُعاءَهُ بِالْخَيْرِ: al-Akhfash said: this is as you say انطلقت انطلاقا, i.e. it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is "like his praying". Abū Jaʿfar said: the omission of the kāf is not something that requires an accusative or anything else; there is no disagreement among the grammarians that one says عمرو كالأسد ("ʿAmr is like the lion"), and if you omit the kāf you say عمرو الأسد. The true account of the verse is that the implied form is: man prays for evil with a praying like his praying for good; then the adjective was put in the place of the noun it qualifies, and the muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the construct) in the place of the muḍāf.

nahhas-irab:12-13.t: وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ آيَتَيْنِ: two objects. Each of them comes in the wake of the other and departs when the other arrives, so they are two signs pointing to One who governs them. فَمَحَوْنا آيَةَ اللَّيْلِ, i.e. We did not give it brightness and light like the light of the day; the thing erased is that which is not clearly seen. وَجَعَلْنا آيَةَ النَّهارِ مُبْصِرَةً: it is the sun and its light. لِتَبْتَغُوا فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ: there is an omission in the speech, i.e. "and that you may rest in the night". وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَصَّلْناهُ تَفْصِيلًا, i.e. We put a separation between one sign and another so that you may take guidance from the proofs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. (كل شيء) is accusative by an implied verb, and likewise وَكُلَّ إِنسانٍ أَلْزَمْناهُ طائِرَهُ فِي عُنُقِهِ. وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ كِتاباً يَلْقاهُ مَنْشُوراً: يلقاه is part of the naʿt (adjective) of كتاب, or if you wish, a ḥāl (circumstantial). We have mentioned the verse and the readings in it.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
اقْرَأْ كِتابَكَ: the sign of the jussive and of indeclinability (bināʾ) is the dropping of the ḍamma from the hamza. It is reported from the Arabs: أقر يا هذا ("read, you!"), with the hamza changed; and from this is the saying of Zuhayr: [al-Ṭawīl] 267-
وإلّا يبد بالظّلم يظلم
(Gloss: "…and whoever does not begin with wrongdoing is wronged" — with يبد for يبدأ.)
كَفى بِنَفْسِكَ is in the position of the nominative, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. حَسِيباً is by way of specification (bayān), or if you wish, a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Isḥāq said: outside the Qurʾan حسيبة is permissible.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
مَنِ اهْتَدى is a protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَإِنَّما يَهْتَدِي لِنَفْسِهِ; and likewise وَمَنْ ضَلَّ فَإِنَّما يَضِلُّ عَلَيْها, i.e. his deeds are his own. This is indicated by وَلا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى, on whose meaning there are two views: one is that no one is held to account for another's sin; the other is that the meaning is: no one should follow another and imitate him in evil, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: إِنَّا وَجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ [al-Zukhruf: 22]. One says وزر يزر, the original being يوزر; the wāw was dropped, according to the Basrans, because it fell between a yāʾ and a kasra. The maṣdar (verbal noun) is وزر, وزر and وزرة.
وَما كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّى نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًا: there are two views on it. One is that the meaning is: We do not punish with the punishment that is a penalty for contravening something that can only be known through being informed, until We send a messenger. The other is that it is the punishment of extermination.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: We have already mentioned وَإِذا أَرَدْنا أَنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أَمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها and the readings in it.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: وَكَمْ is in the position of the accusative, governed by أهلكنا.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: مَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ الْعاجِلَةَ, i.e. who does not want reward in the Hereafter, We do not withhold that from him — لِمَنْ نُرِيدُ.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: كُلًّا is accusative by نمدّ. هؤُلاءِ is a badal (substitute) for كلّ. وَهَؤُلاءِ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it, i.e. We provide for the believer and the unbeliever. وَما كانَ عَطاءُ رَبِّكَ مَحْظُوراً: Saʿīd said, from Qatāda: i.e. diminished.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: كَيْفَ is in the position of the accusative, governed by فضّلنا, except that it is indeclinable (mabnī), not inflected. وَلَلْآخِرَةُ أَكْبَرُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). دَرَجاتٍ is in the position of the accusative by way of specification (bayān), and likewise تَفْضِيلًا. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: whoever of the people of Paradise is high sees his superiority over whoever is below him, and whoever is beneath him does not see that anyone above him is better than he.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: فَتَقْعُدَ is accusative as the reply to the prohibition.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ إِحْساناً: a maṣdar (verbal noun). إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الْكِبَرَ is the reading of the people of Medina, the people of Basra and ʿĀṣim; the reading of the people of Kufa except ʿĀṣim is (إمّا يبلغانّ عندك الكبر). The first reading is clearer in Arabic, because أحدهما is singular. The second is permissible, as you say جاءاني أحدهما أو كلاهما ("they came to me, one of them or both of them") as a badal (substitute), because after the verb you have brought in three; the proper form is جاءني أحدهما أو كلاهما. If you wish you may say جاءاني كلاهما أو أحدهما, with كلاهما as tawkīd (emphasis) and أحدهما conjoined.
فَلا تَقُلْ لَهُما أُفٍّ: there are seven dialectal forms of it. Al-Ḥasan and the people of Medina read (ولا تقل لهما أفّ) «[Translator's note: so printed, with ولا for فلا.]» with kasra and tanwīn (nunation); Abū ʿAmr and the people of Kufa said it with kasra and without tanwīn; the people of Mecca and the people of Syria read it with fatḥa and without tanwīn. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash reported three dialectal forms besides these:
they reported the accusative with tanwīn, the ḍamma with tanwīn, and the ḍamma without tanwīn. Al-Akhfash reported the seventh form; he said: one says أفّي, with the yāʾ retained, as if he said "this saying is for you". Abū Jaʿfar said: in the first reading the kasra is because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the tanwīn because it is indefinite, to distinguish it from the definite; it is a good reading, and the basic rule when two quiescent letters meet is kasra. Al-Aṣmaʿī claimed that in such words only tanwīn is permissible, and that Dhū al-Rumma made an error in his saying: [al-Ṭawīl] 268-
وقفنا فقلنا إيه عن أمّ سالم ... وما بال تكليم الدّيار البلاقع
(Gloss: "We halted and said: 'Tell on (īh) about Umm Sālim!' — yet what use is speaking to empty, desolate dwellings?")
Al-Aṣmaʿī was fond of rejecting rare dialectal forms that are not frequent in the speech of the eloquent. As for the skilled grammarians, they say: the tanwīn is dropped on the basis that it is definite, and on this basis are the second reading and the third reading — because the fatḥa is light and the doubling heavy — and the tanwīn is as explained above. The ḍamma without tanwīn is by assimilation (itbāʿ), as one says ردّ; and the tanwīn is as we mentioned, except that al-Akhfash said: tanwīn is ugly when you put it in the nominative, because there is no lām with it in the speech — as if he takes its nominative to be as a mubtadaʾ (subject), as one says ويل له ("woe to him"); and he claimed that the accusative with tanwīn is as one says تعسا له ("may he perish").
وَقُلْ لَهُما قَوْلًا كَرِيماً, i.e. a speech with which you honour them and show them reverence.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ, i.e. from the relative, the orphans, the poor and the wayfarer. ابْتِغاءَ رَحْمَةٍ: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. seeking provision that you are waiting for. فَقُلْ لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَيْسُوراً: it is said: with gentleness, softness and a promise.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t:
وَلا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلى عُنُقِكَ: اليد (the hand) is feminine, and العنق (the neck) is treated as masculine and as feminine, masculine being more common, as the poet said: [al-Rajaz] 269-
في سرطم هاد وعنق عرطل
(Gloss: "…with a long gullet, a forward-reaching [head], and a long neck.")
The ḍamma in عنق was dropped because of its heaviness.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ, i.e. He restricts, and does of that whatever contains what is right. This is indicated by إِنَّهُ كانَ بِعِبادِهِ خَبِيراً, i.e. He knows what is good for them. On the meaning of «فتقعد ملوما محسورا» there are two views. One is that of al-Farrāʾ: it is in the status of المحسور, i.e. the worn-out, exhausted one; he reported: حسرت الدّابة فهي محسورة وحسير ("I exhausted the riding animal, so it is exhausted"), when you drive it until it breaks down. The other view is that «محسورا» means one who has been overtaken by regret (ḥasra).

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كانَ خِطْأً: خطأ is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, its noun is latent (muḍmar) in it, and the clause is the khabar of inna. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned the readings in it.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: وَلا تَقْرَبُوا الزِّنى: some of the Arabs lengthen it, making it a maṣdar (verbal noun) of زانى, because it only happens between two. إِنَّهُ كانَ فاحِشَةً وَساءَ سَبِيلًا: سبيلا is by way of specification (bayān), i.e. its path is evil and its act foul.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t:
وَلا تَقْتُلُوا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ: we have mentioned it. وَمَنْ قُتِلَ مَظْلُوماً فَقَدْ: مظلوما is a ḥāl (circumstantial). فَقَدْ جَعَلْنا: assimilation (idghām) is good, because the dāl is from the tip of the tongue and the jīm from its middle, so they are close to each other; pronouncing it distinctly is permissible. لِوَلِيِّهِ, i.e. the person nearest to him. سُلْطاناً: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: every سلطان in the Qurʾan is a proof. Abū Isḥāq said: whoever read فَلا يُسْرِفْ فِي الْقَتْلِ made it a statement, i.e. the killer of his kinsman is not to go to excess. «[Translator's note: the statement form would be فلا يسرفُ; the source prints the jussive vowelling.]» إِنَّهُ كانَ مَنْصُوراً: there are five views on the pronoun:
it may refer to the next of kin (al-walī), and this is the most fitting in the view of the people of reasoning, because it is the nearest to it. Ibn Kathīr said, from Mujāhid: the slain man was helped; and this is a good view, because the slain man was helped in this world when the killing of his killer was commanded, and in the Hereafter by an abundant reward and the punishment of his killer. It is said: the killing was helped. Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning may be "the killing", because it is an act. «[Translator's note: the source names four positions explicitly before the fifth.]» The fifth view is that of Abū ʿUbayd; he said: it may be that the first killer was helped when he killed. This is the most far-fetched and most strained of them.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: وَأَوْفُوا بِالْعَهْدِ إِنَّ الْعَهْدَ كانَ مَسْؤُلًا: everything Allah has commanded is included in this, because He has made a covenant with us concerning it.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
وَلا تَقْفُ ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ: included in this is the prohibition of slandering chaste women, of saying about people what one does not know, and of speaking about law and religion on the basis of conjecture, and that no one should say what is not his right. إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤادَ كُلُّ أُولئِكَ كانَ عَنْهُ مَسْؤُلًا: included in this is the prohibition of listening to what it is not lawful to listen to, and of intending and resolving upon what it is not lawful to look at; know that a person is questioned about all of that. He said أولئك of things other than people, because for everything pointed to that is at a distance you may say أولئك, as the poet said: [al-Kāmil] 270-
ذمّ المنازل غير منزلة اللّوى ... والعيش بعد أولئك الأيّام
(Gloss: "Blame all dwellings except the dwelling of al-Liwā, and life after those days.")

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
وَلا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحاً, i.e. possessing exultation. Yaʿqūb the reader reported مَرَحاً with kasra on the rāʾ «[Translator's note: i.e. مَرِحاً; the source prints the ordinary vowelling.]» as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Akhfash said: the kasra on the rāʾ is better, because it is the active participle. Abū Isḥāq said:
the fatḥa on the rāʾ is better, because it contains the sense of emphasis, as one says جاء فلان ركضا ("So-and-so came running"); he made it a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl. المرح in the language is insolence and arrogant exultation, and from it come strutting and haughtiness. إِنَّكَ لَنْ تَخْرِقَ الْأَرْضَ, i.e. your strength will never reach this. وَلَنْ تَبْلُغَ الْجِبالَ طُولًا: so one should not be haughty and exalt oneself.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: «[Translator's note: the entry begins mid-discussion, apparently concerning those who read سَيِّئُهُ (rather than سَيِّئَةً) in كُلُّ ذلِكَ كانَ سَيِّئُهُ.]» They argued from good things that came before, among them وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ إِحْساناً and among them وَقُلْ لَهُما قَوْلًا كَرِيماً; and Abū Ḥātim argued from His saying «مكروها», not مكروهة. Abū Jaʿfar said: nothing follows from these arguments, because the good things came earlier in the section of commands; then came the prohibition, and after it came كُلُّ ذلِكَ كانَ سَيِّئُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهاً, referring to what was forbidden. And He said مكروها and not مكروهة because it refers back to the wording of كلّ, and it is a second khabar (predicate) of the latent pronoun in كان, and that pronoun is masculine.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: إِنَّكُمْ لَتَقُولُونَ قَوْلًا: a maṣdar (verbal noun) containing the sense of emphasis. عَظِيماً is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: Abū Isḥāq said: وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنا, i.e. We have indeed made clear. He said: and the meaning of وَما يَزِيدُهُمْ is: the making clear does not increase them إِلَّا نُفُوراً.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
«[Translator's note: the entry refers to عُلُوًّا كَبِيراً, a maṣdar of a different form from its verb تعالى.]» I.e. تعاليا, as the poet said: [al-Wāfir] 271-
وليس بأن تتبّعه اتّباعا
(Gloss: "…and it is not by your following him with a following" — with the maṣdar اتّباع of a different form from the verb تتبّع.)

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ السَّماواتُ السَّبْعُ: with the feminine on the basis of the group, and يسبح with the masculine on the basis of the whole. وَإِنْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ: the scholars have discussed its meaning. Some of them said: it is the glorification that is known; some said: it is particular (restricted); and some said: its glorification is its pointing to Allah's transcendence, Mighty and Majestic, and they interpreted وَلكِنْ لا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ as an address to the unbelievers who do not draw the inference. It is said:
"but you do not understand" is an address to people in general, and since among them are some who do not understand that, [it is said that] they did not understand. إِنَّهُ كانَ حَلِيماً, i.e. forbearing towards those who do not draw the inference. غَفُوراً to whoever of them repents.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
It is said: these were people who, when they heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting in Mecca to call people, would revile him; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed him that He would put a barrier between them and him so that they would not understand his recitation. Al-Akhfash said:
«مستورا» means ساترا ("concealing"); the passive pattern مفعول may have the meaning of the active فاعل, as one says مشؤوم and ميمون, i.e. شائم and يامن «[Translator's note: printed «ويا من», evidently for «ويامن».]», because the veil is what conceals. Someone else said: the veil is literally "concealed", because it is something hidden from them.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: وَلَّوْا عَلى أَدْبارِهِمْ نُفُوراً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), on the basis that it is the plural of نافر; and it may be singular on the basis that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: وَإِذْ هُمْ نَجْوى: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the implied form is: ذو نجوى ("people of secret counsel").

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: انْظُرْ كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لَكَ الْأَمْثالَ, i.e. they said at one time "he is deluded" and at another "he is a sorcerer", to attach falsehood to you. فَضَلُّوا from the path of truth, فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلًا to it.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: خَلْقاً: a maṣdar (verbal noun). جَدِيداً is its naʿt (adjective). جديد has one meaning for masculine and feminine; جديدة for the feminine is a poor dialectal usage according to Sībawayh.

nahhas-irab:50-51.t: قُلْ كُونُوا حِجارَةً أَوْ حَدِيداً أَوْ خَلْقاً مِمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِي صُدُورِكُمْ, i.e. imagine whatever you wish; you must die and be resurrected. These verses were among the greatest proofs of the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: فَسَيَقُولُونَ مَنْ يُعِيدُنا — so He, Mighty and Majestic, foretold that they would say this, and foretold that they would shake their heads in deeming what He said to them unlikely, and that they would say, along with shaking their heads or after it: مَتى هُوَ. And it was recited to them «[Translator's note: printed «وتلى», for «وتُلي».]», and the matter turned out just so.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: يَوْمَ يَدْعُوكُمْ فَتَسْتَجِيبُونَ بِحَمْدِهِ: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: people will come out of their graves saying "Glory be to You, and with Your praise". وَتَظُنُّونَ إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا: it is said: they only thought this after the reality which creation cannot escape.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t:
وَقُلْ لِعِبادِي يَقُولُوا الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ, i.e. the statement which is best. Al-Māzinī said: the meaning is:
"Say to My servants: 'Say', and they will say." إنّ الشيطان ينزغ بينهم, i.e. he incites the unbelievers against the believers.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: قُلِ ادْعُوا الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ: there is an omission in the speech, indicated by what follows; the implied form is: "Say: call on those whom you claimed to be your gods besides Allah, and let them remove harm from you and shift you from straitness and hardship to ease." This is indicated by فَلا يَمْلِكُونَ كَشْفَ الضُّرِّ عَنْكُمْ وَلا تَحْوِيلًا, i.e. they will not shift you from straitness and hardship to ease and plenty.
